findings.claim: The statement of 'Arc descent gives formal glueing' is false as written and is not the cited theorem. It forms the square with F(A[1/f]) and F(A'[1/f]) for an arbitrary f ∈ I, whereas formal glueing uses Spec(A) ∖ V(I) and Spec(A') ∖ V(IA'). It omits that I is finitely generated and that A/I^n ≅ A'/I^nA' for every n. Its hypothesis '(I-complete) arc descent' is not Bhatt–Mathew's: their Theorem 6.4 is for arc-sheaves on qcqs schemes, finitary and valued in an ∞-category compactly generated by cotruncated objects, and Corollary 6.7 covers all arc-sheaves. The paper applies it only to étale cohomology, which is a plain arc sheaf by Theorem 2.2.5. Counterexample to the item: take k algebraically closed, ℓ ≠ char k, F = RΓ_ét(−, ℤ/ℓ) (an arc sheaf), A = k[x], I = (x), A' = k[[x]] (so A/I^n ≅ A'/I^n) and f = x(x−1) ∈ I. Then A'[1/f] = k((x)), and the square is Cartesian iff RΓ_{V(f)}(A) → RΓ_{V(f)}(A') is an isomorphism. But H^2_{V(f)}(𝔸^1, ℤ/ℓ) = H^1(𝔸^1 ∖ {0,1}, ℤ/ℓ) = (ℤ/ℓ)^2 (Kummer classes of x and x−1), while H^2 with support in the closed point of k[[x]] is H^1(k((x)), ℤ/ℓ) = ℤ/ℓ. The restriction kills the class of x−1, an ℓ-th power in k[[x]]. Also: The item states formal glueing with the square F(A), F(A'), F(A[1/f]), F(A'[1/f]) 'for f ∈ I' when A/I^n ≅ A'/I^n. That is false and is not what the cited theorem says. Take f = 0 ∈ I: the square then asserts F(A) ≅ F(A'). With A = Z → A' = Z_p, I = (p) (so A/I^n ≅ A'/I^n) and F = RΓ_ét(−, Z/2), which satisfies arc descent (item 026), this would give H^1_ét(Spec Z, Z/2) ≅ H^1_ét(Spec Z_p, Z/2). The left side is 0 (Minkowski) and the right side is H^1(F_p, Z/2) = Z/2. It fails for nonzero f as well. With A = C[x, y, 1/(y−1)], I = (x, y), A' = C[[x, y]] and f = x, the square would force RΓ_{V(x)}(A, Z/ℓ) ≅ RΓ_{V(x)}(A', Z/ℓ). By purity H^3 of these is H^1 of V(x) with Z/ℓ(−1) coefficients, and V(x) is A^1 ∖ {1} on one side and Spec C[[y]] on the other. Bhatt–Mathew's theorem uses the punctured spectra Spec(A) ∖ V(I), which equal Spec(A[1/f]) only for I = (f). It is also stated for arc sheaves, not for 'I-complete arc descent'. Every use in this paper is along a principal ideal: a in Lemma 5.4.2, p in Theorem 5.5.1, ϖ in Theorem 2.2.7. The item also duplicates the Bhatt–Mathew extraction's items without saying so; compare item 029, whose note does.

Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, arXiv 1807.04725v4, Definition 1.14: 'A formal glueing datum is given by a pair (R → S, I) where R → S is a map of commutative rings and I ⊂ R is a finitely generated ideal such that R/I^n ≃ S/I^nS for all n ≥ 0 … square Spec(S) ∖ V(IS) → Spec(S), Spec(R) ∖ V(I) → Spec(R)'. Theorem 6.4: 'Let 𝒞 be an ∞-category that is compactly generated by cotruncated objects. Let ℱ: Sch_{qcqs,R}^op → 𝒞 be a finitary arc-sheaf. Then ℱ satisfies formal glueing'. Then F satisfies formal glueing, i.e., if (A → B, I) is a formal glueing datum … then the natural square F(Spec(A)) → F(Spec(B)), F(Spec(A) ∖ V(I)) → F(Spec(B) ∖ V(IB)) is cartesian.' findings.evidence: Paper, Theorem 5.3.5, p. 59: 'For a prime p, a ring R, a commutative, finite, locally free R-group G of p-power order, and an animated R-algebra A such that π0(A) is p-Henselian, RΓ(A,G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ(A/^L p^n, G)'. Corollary 5.3.7, p. 61: 'let G be a commutative, finite, locally free R-group of p-power order. For each animated R-algebra A such that π0(A) is p-Henselian, H^i(A,G) ≅ 0 for i ≥ 3 (resp. … for i ≥ 2 if (π0(A)/(p))^red is perfect)'. The brief reads: 'Theorem 5.3.5 (p-adic continuity RΓ(A, G) ≅ R lim RΓ(A/^L p^n, G) for p-Henselian π_0(A)), Corollary 5.3.7 (H^{≥3} = 0, and H^{≥2} = 0 when (π_0 A/p)^red is perfect)'. Counterexample to the brief's Corollary 5.3.7: take p = 3, R = ℤ_3, G = ℤ/2 (finite étale, so finite locally free and smooth), and A the 3-adic completion of ℤ_3[x^{±1}, y^{±1}, z^{±1}]. A is 3-adically complete, hence 3-Henselian. By Grothendieck's comparison and Gabber's affine proper base change, H^3_fppf(A, ℤ/2) = H^3_ét(A, ℤ/2) ≅ H^3_ét(𝔽_3[x^{±1}, y^{±1}, z^{±1}], ℤ/2). The cup product is nonzero because its pullback to 𝔽̄_3 generates H^3(𝔾_m^3, ℤ/2) ≅ Λ^3((ℤ/2)^3) by Künneth. The same construction with the perfection of 𝔽_3[x^{±1}, y^{±1}] gives H^2 ≠ 0 with (A/p)^red perfect.

findings.claim: Item 115 merges Corollaries 5.6.10, 5.6.12 and 5.6.13 and Example 5.6.11 into one statement and loses hypotheses on the way. Since Pic(R') = 0, H^2(R', μ_2) ↪ Br(R'), so a lift of the class to H^2(R, μ_2) maps to 0, and H^2(R, μ_2) → H^2(R', μ_2) is not injective. The paper uses it in the statement of Theorem 2.2.5, in Remark 2.2.6, in the proofs of Theorem 2.3.4 and Corollary 2.3.7, and throughout Section 5. Mathlib has only the predicate 'Henselian pair'. No atlas stage plans the Henselization of a pair: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian plans affinoid henselizations, and Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 4 plans strict henselisation of local rings. Also: §5.3 rests on three facts about Henselian pairs, and no item covers any of them. (i) Every pair (A, I) has an I-Henselization: ind-étale, iso modulo I, and faithfully flat when I lies in the Jacobson radical. Lemma 5.3.1, Claim 5.3.5.3 and Corollary 5.3.8 use it. (ii) For a Henselian pair (A, I) and a smooth affine Q, Q(A) → Q(A/I) is surjective (Elkik / Stacks 07M7 together with the Henselian property). Theorem 5.3.5 uses it. (iii) Étale algebras lift along surjections (Stacks 04D1). Theorem 5.3.5 uses it. Mathlib at 082e2d3 has only the definition HenselianRing (RingTheory/Henselian.lean:94): no Henselization and no lifting of smooth sections. The only atlas stage on Henselian pairs is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian, which is about affinoid (Huber) Henselizations. Other extractions already itemize exactly these inputs: Clausen–Mathew–Morrow /043 (characterizations, including the lifting property against étale maps), /044 (Elkik's theorem) and /046 (Henselization of pairs), routed as a source to SchemeAndStackFoundations; and Clausen–Mathew /111. Also: The p-Henselization S^h_(p) of an animated ring is used throughout this share: Lemma 5.4.2 step (1), Theorem 5.5.2, Corollary 5.5.3 (where it is part of the statement of item 105), Lemma 5.6.5 and Theorem 5.7.2. It is defined via Proposition 5.2.4 as the ind-étale lift of π_0(S)^h_(p). It comes with the Cartesian square RΓ(S) → RΓ(S^h_(p)) over RΓ(S[1/p]) → RΓ(S^h_(p)[1/p]). Neither the construction nor the square is an item. Item 087 (Proposition 5.2.4) records only the equivalence of étale sites. The Henselization of a ring along an ideal is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: the declaration index has no 'henseliz' entry. No atlas stage constructs it for general pairs; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:henselian is about affinoid Henselizations.

findings.claim: R03.3 plans regular sequences and depth for Noetherian local rings, but it says nothing about local cohomology or cohomology with supports. The item's essential use is non-Noetherian: H^i_Z(A, M) = 0 below the length of a regular sequence for W(R_∞) and A_inf(A). The item's own note concedes this 'must be included there', which is a request, not a plan. The report goes further and says R03.3 plans 'the vanishing of local cohomology along a regular sequence'; its description does not. The cited Mathlib declaration is only the Ext-colimit definition. It has no long exact sequence and no comparison with sheaf cohomology with supports, and that comparison fails for general non-Noetherian rings. Also: Item 063 is used in the proofs of Theorems 6.1.2 and 6.2.7. It is marked 'planned' at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3, and Mathlib's localCohomology is cited. Neither covers what the paper uses. The paper needs H^i_Z(A_inf(A), M) as cohomology with supports in an arbitrary closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), over the non-Noetherian A_inf(A) and the tilt R̂_∞^♭, together with its long exact sequence for the decreasing induction. R03.3 plans no local cohomology at all: it covers regular sequences, depth and the complete-intersection criteria of Noetherian patching. findings.claim: The item says a square-zero extension with ideal M is the pullback A ×_{A⊕M[1]} A along a derivation s, 'equivalently a map L_{A/A'} → M[1]'. The paper does not say this, and the equivalence is false. A map L_{A/A'} → M[1] is an A'-linear derivation. It gives a commutative square (5.1.9.1), but the square need not be Cartesian. findings.claim: The proof asserts that the iterated derived a_j-adic completion of A^i = ∏ V_s 'is the product of a subset of the valuation rings comprising A^i'. That holds only when the surviving V_s are already a-adically complete. Lemma 2.2.3 and the proof supply 'p-adically complete valuation rings of dimension ≤ 1', and in characteristic p this condition is empty. Characteristic p is exactly the case Theorem 5.7.2 applies the lemma in, with A a perfect F_p-algebra. A rank-one valuation ring of characteristic p with algebraically closed fraction field need not be complete; take the integral closure of F_p[[t]] in an algebraic closure of F_p((t)). Derived completion commutes with products, so the completion is ∏ \hat{V_s} over the s where no a_j becomes a unit. Each \hat{V_s} is again a rank ≤ 1 valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field (Bhatt–Mathew Proposition 6.2), so it is perfectoid and the argument goes through.
